frontier.hypothesis: The DA shape (byte offset routed through `idx`, sum in `wid`) is the only untried-in-detail form that satisfies all three constraints simultaneously; its whole 12-point cost is that `idx` and `idx2` are swapped between $s0 and $s1, and the target's own allocation proves the wanted state is reachable.
frontier.mechanism: local_alloc runs before global_alloc. In the shipped/CA shape the block-local byte-offset CSE temp lives across all four rand() calls, needs a callee-save, and claims $s0, pushing the block-local `idx2` to $s1; the multi-block `idx` then re-uses $s0 because its range does not overlap. In DA that claimant is gone, so `idx2` takes $s0 from local_alloc and `idx` is left $s1 by global_alloc.

frontier.hypothesis: The shipped 1-point residual (`addu s0,s0,s1` vs target `addu s0,s1,s0`) can be defeated by changing how the assignment is EXPANDED rather than how it is spelled.
frontier.mechanism: optabs.c:399-417 (expand_binop) swaps a commutative operand pair whenever the expansion `target == op1`. Eight source-level respellings are already measured dead (previous session's H11) and the swapped form is present in the .rtl dump before cse runs. What has not been probed is which C constructs cause expand_binop to be called with `target == 0` (an anonymous temp) so no swap test fires, with the temp later coalesced into `idx`'s register.
frontier.next_probe: Read expr.c's expand_expr / expand_assignment store path to enumerate the constructs that expand a binop into a fresh temp rather than directly into the destination pseudo (compound assignment through a cast, a differently-typed or narrower view of the destination, an assignment used as a value), then sandbox each on the shipped body.

frontier.hypothesis: All three shapes are exactly one instruction away and each fails on a DIFFERENT fully-named GCC decision, which is the signature of a shape that is close to but not the original — the original's inner-loop pseudo set or live-range shape differs from all three.
frontier.mechanism: The target's 78 instructions imply a specific pseudo count and live-range structure in the inner-loop block and in the found-slot arm; comparing the three near-miss builds' scheduler and allocator state against what the target implies should show which pseudo none of them reproduces.
